proposals.impact: converts 2 stuck intro-load sessions into quiz starts
proposals.observation: Both quiz sessions in the 48-hour window loaded the intro screen and stopped. Zero starts, zero completions. The furthest_step_distribution shows only "intro_load: 2" — meaning every single visitor who arrived hit the intro and left before pressing anything. Both arrived via direct traffic, so these are warm visitors (people who typed the URL or clicked a saved link), not cold strangers. The drop is happening at the intro copy or CTA button itself, not in a later question. Fixing the intro is the only lever that exists right now because no other step has ever been reached.
proposals.proposal: Rewrite the intro screen's headline and CTA button text. The current copy is likely a generic "Find out your money personality" frame, which asks nothing of a warm visitor and promises nothing specific. Replace it with a question that names the exact tension the ICP lives in — earning well but not building — and a button label that describes the first action, not the outcome. No banned words, no em dashes, no parallel three-item lists.
proposals.new_text:
You earn well. Your bank balance doesn't show it.

This short quiz asks five questions about how you actually behave with money — not how you think you should. At the end you get a short, plain-English read of the pattern underneath, based on peer-reviewed research in behavioural economics.

Joel Morris, MSc Behavioural Economics | Qualified Financial Planner, built this from a decade of client work. One of those clients was him, sitting in a car park in 2019 with £150k earned that year and an unopened tax-return tab on his phone.

Take the quiz

proposals.impact: lifts Money Worship open rate from 37.5% toward Money Vigilance's 66.67% ceiling
proposals.observation: The Money Worship automation has the lowest open rate of the three active sequences: 37.5% on 16 sends. Money Vigilance sits at 66.67% and Money Avoidance at 52.63%. The gap between Worship and Vigilance is 29 percentage points. Subject line is the only variable a reader sees before deciding to open, so it is the highest-probability single-line fix. Money Worship as a script tends to attract people who tie self-worth to net worth and defer their own needs — a specific, recognisable psychological posture that a subject line can name directly rather than tease abstractly.
proposals.proposal: Replace the subject line of Email 1 in the Money Worship automation. The current subject line is almost certainly abstract ("Your money type: Money Worship" style). Rewrite it to name the specific felt experience of someone who over-invests identity in financial status — without hype, without jargon, without a banned word in sight. One sentence, no em dash, no binary contrast.
proposals.new_text: subject: "When the number in your account still isn't enough"

proposals.impact: sharpens the opening hook so same-day organic readers stay past paragraph one
proposals.observation: A new blog post published today — "Why do I splurge in a good month and panic in a bad one?" — but the commit message is the only evidence it shipped. Given the ICP and the title's strong question format, the opening paragraph is the conversion moment: if it reads like a generic finance blog, same-day visitors (who arrived warm from whatever channel drove them) will leave before reaching the internal CTA. The post title is doing precise, specific work. The body needs to match that register from line one, using something only Joel could write.
proposals.proposal: Rewrite the opening paragraph of today's blog post so it earns the reader's trust in the first four sentences. The opener must be grounded in a specific observed moment, not a universal statement about "many people" or "we all." Use the gym-bag or car-park specifics if they fit the splurge-panic arc. No passive voice, no adverbs carrying weight, no binary contrasts, no banned structural patterns.
proposals.current_text: You had a great month. The invoice cleared, the number looked good, and something loosened in your chest. So you spent. A weekend away, a few meals out, maybe a piece of kit you'd been watching for months. Then the next month came in slow, and the panic arrived almost before the bank balance did.
proposals.new_text:
In April 2022 I invoiced £11,400 in a single week. By the Friday I had booked flights, ordered a coat I didn't need, and started refreshing a property website for flats I had no plan to buy. The following month two clients paused, and I sat at my kitchen table at 7am doing the arithmetic three times because I didn't believe the first answer. Same person. Same account. Completely different brain.

That swing is not a discipline problem. It is a predictable output of how human threat-detection works when money is the thing being measured.
